thread:
marie: Heads-up — noticed a weird late-binding issue after the eu-west-2 subnet split. Some GPU allocs are getting pinned to the old subnet tag and ending up on shared pools instead of dedicated carveouts. Causing noisy-neighbor spikes for a couple tenants.

tony: any example allocation IDs / logs?

marie: here’s one from last night (shortened):
```
2026-03-18T03:12:45Z scheduler: bind_attempt id=alloc-8a7f tenant=acme user=svc-obs
2026-03-18T03:12:45Z scheduler: node_candidate node=eu-west-2b-n045 labels={subnet:v1,gpu_pool:shared}
2026-03-18T03:12:45Z scheduler: late_bind re-eval -> node=eu-west-2b-n045 labels={subnet:v2,gpu_pool:dedicated-acme}
2026-03-18T03:12:45Z rpc: route_commit node=eu-west-2b-n045 -> assigned_pool=shared
2026-03-18T03:12:46Z runtime: start_inference worker=xx gpu=0 tenant=acme
```
Looks like the scheduler re-evaluated to a v2 node but the routing layer still committed the older pool id.

zane: that's interesting — sounds like a race between the late-bind check and the route-commit write. The commit path currently reads the node label snapshot from cache which is updated async after subnet-controller reconciles. If the subnet split updated the node label recently, cache staleness could point to old pool.

aya: can we force a read-after-write or TTL 0 for label cache on bind if node label version < alloc.version? Cheap guard.

tony: quick mitigation: add a pre-commit validation that re-reads node labels from k/v before finalizing route_assign. If mismatch -> retry bind (fast path), or fallback to dedicated carveout routing if tenant has reservation.

marie: agree. downside: extra RPC in hot path. We measured ~2ms extra per bind in test, but the bigger worry is transient double-allocation when we retry — that inflates cost and GPU occupancy for a few seconds. Our cost model shows a ~4-8% bump on reschedule-heavy windows.

zane: what about optimistic update + compensating cleanup? i.e., commit route with tentative tag and then reconcile once cache catches up; if mismatch, reassign quietly and notify ops. That avoids immediate retry churn.

aya: but that can lead to tenant ending up on shared pool for N seconds which breaks isolation guarantees for enterprise customers. Not acceptable for Dedicated customers.

marie: true. A split approach might work: for reserved/dedicated tenants, force sync check and retry on mismatch. For best-effort/shared tenants, use optimistic commit to reduce latency.

tony: patch proposal sketched below. Rolling controller change to binder:
```
if tenant.reservation == "dedicated":
  node_label = node_api.read_labels_strict(node)
  if node_label.subnet != alloc.expected_subnet:
    raise RetryBind
else:
  // existing fast path uses cache
  node_label = cache.get(node)
  if node_label.subnet != alloc.expected_subnet:
    // allow optimistic commit + reconcile
    route.commit(tentative=True)
```
Canary: deploy to ap-south first (low critical load) then eu-west-2.

zane: canary in ap-south is fine but watch capacity — ap-south has limited dedicated slices; we should ensure the canary does not allocate reserved GPUs. Use test tenants only.

infra-bot: deploy job started: binder-v2.3.1-canary -> cluster: ap-south-1 (job id: job-6721) :rocket:

aya: also add telemetry: emit 'latebind_cache_mismatch' metric with fields {tenant_type, region, alloc_id}. We need to track frequency and cost delta per event.

marie: agreed. added to issue tracker for billing team to approximate cost impact per mutation.

tony: follow-up: we should also add a controller that invalidates the cache for nodes when subnet-controller updates labels. That reduces staleness without per-bind RPC. TTL tune + explicit invalidation on label-change seems best.

zane: I'll own the cache invalidation hook. Plan: on Node label change event -> publish invalidation to binder cache topic. Binder subscribes and invalidates specific node key. Fall back to strict read if invalidation hasn't arrived after X ms.

marie: thanks. timeline?

zane: prototype by EOD tomorrow, canary in 48h, full rollout next week if metrics look good.

marie: perfect. will update impacted tenants and CS for potential transient billing blips.

aya: thumbs-up. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: note: created incident-3456 (informational) to track noisy neighbor reports and mitigations.
